item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find reliable 2024 reporting showing Abiy or his close circle submitting to independent probes of assets, campaign finance, conflicts of interest, or hidden official decisions. I also did not find credible evidence of a serious independent investigation into the PM’s associates that the government welcomed or protected. The available record is mainly about pressure on watchdogs and narrow formal accountability language, not real openness.","evidence":[{"title":"Actors of protection: Ethiopia","publisher":"GOV.UK","date":"2024-01-12","url":"https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ethiopia-country-policy-and-information-notes/country-policy-and-information-note-actors-of-protection-ethiopia-february-2024-accessible","summary":"The note says the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission receives complaints and that some state and federal institutions implemented recommendations on human-rights protections and prison conditions. This is weak evidence of some complaint-handling capacity, but it does not show robust independence or access to sensitive investigations.","question_ids":["7B.6"]},{"title":"Transitional justice policy launch","publisher":"ENA English","date":"2024-12-14","url":"https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5626876","summary":"The government framed transitional justice around accountability, truth-seeking, conditional amnesty, reconciliation, and institutional reform after consultations with civil society and vulnerable groups. This is roadmap rhetoric, not proof of independent investigation, but it is the clearest official commitment to truth-seeking in 2024.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.5"]},{"title":"ICRC bulletin on Ethiopia","publisher":"International Committee of the Red Cross","date":"2024-09-13","url":"https://www.icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024","summary":"The ICRC said it maintained dialogue and training on IHL/IHRL for the ENDF, police, militias, and other armed groups. That is limited rule-of-law engagement, though it is training rather than independent investigation or accountability.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.2"]},{"title":"Final observation report on June 24 rerun elections","publisher":"CECOE","date":"2024","url":"https://cecoe.org/download/final-observation-report-on-the-outstanding-and-reelections-of-the-sixth-general-elections-held-in-benishangul-gumuz-afar-somali-and-central-ethiopia-regions-in-june-24-2024/","summary":"Domestic observers described the reruns as transparent enough for systematic observation, with broad observer deployment and monitoring of polling, counting, and the post-election environment. This shows some tolerance for outside monitoring, but only in a narrow electoral context.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.5"]},{"title":"Ethiopia authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-02-19","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/","summary":"Amnesty said emergency powers were used for warrantless arrests, movement limits, and bans on assemblies and associations, and noted the extension was not transparently published. That is direct evidence against tolerating scrutiny or independent reporting.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.2"]},{"title":"Ethiopia’s deepening crackdown on dissent","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-03-04","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/04/ethiopias-deepening-crackdown-dissent","summary":"HRW reported arbitrary arrests of opposition figures and journalists and said no one appeared safe from arbitrary detention. This is strong evidence that the state did not tolerate independent scrutiny of official conduct.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.2"]},{"title":"Ethiopia halt crackdown against human rights groups","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-06-18","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/ethiopia-halt-crackdown-against-human-rights-groups","summary":"HRW said security and intelligence personnel followed, intimidated, and threatened human-rights workers, including at homes and offices. That directly chills independent investigation and watchdog activity.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.2","7B.5"]},{"title":"Ethiopian authorities suspend three rights groups","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-12-02","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/ethiopia-authorities-suspend-three-rights-groups","summary":"HRW said Abiy publicly praised reforms like media freedom and NGO registration while the government kept suspending and cracking down on rights groups. This is a clear rhetoric-versus-practice gap and weighs strongly against tolerance for independent oversight.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.2","7B.5"]},{"title":"Reuters investigation via EHRC: secret committee orders killings and arrests","publisher":"Reuters via EHRC","date":"2024-02-27","url":"https://ehrc.org/in-ethiopia-a-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels-reuters/","summary":"Reuters reported a secret “Koree Nageenyaa” committee that interfered in the justice system and was tied to widespread human-rights violations. That implies opaque decision-making and resistance to independent investigation of politically protected actors.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.2","7B.5"]},{"title":"Abiy says rights body hijacked by foreigners","publisher":"AFP via EWN","date":"2024-07-04","url":"https://www.ewn.co.za/2024/07/04/ethiopias-abiy-says-rights-body-hijacked-by-foreigners","summary":"Abiy’s “foreign hijacking” claim is delegitimizing rhetoric toward oversight institutions. It reads as blame-shifting and hostility to scrutiny rather than cooperation with independent investigation.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.2"]}]}
